authoredFrom: SQLD3 (M60 SQL wave, 2026-09-26). Authored from the grammar's own layout, probed by bb_tests/sql/probe/field-introspection.mts ('function argument w/ custom type', 'function returns shapes'): function_argument has no `type` field, only `custom_type`, so a builtin type is positional — the child after the name — and `keyword_in`/`keyword_out`/`keyword_inout` sit BEFORE the name. Return types are the span after keyword_returns up to function_body or function_language. Expectations written from that probe, not from the analyzer's output.
comment: Every type string is the source's own spelling (read out of the node text), so `int[]` and `numeric(10,2)` and `timestamp with time zone` pin spacing too. The `direction` rows are the regression pin for the fabricated `type: "IN"`.
note: `forbidParameters.types` is the channel that catches the mode keyword being read as a type — an expect-only pin passes unchanged when `a`'s type is `IN` instead of `integer`, because the pin never looks at the value it should not have.
